sanskrit: tathaiva rājā vṛṣṇīnām ugrasenaḥ pratāpavān upagīyamāno gandharvaiḥ strīsahasrasahāyavān
english: Likewise the mighty king of the Vṛṣṇis, Ugrasena the illustrious, was being extolled by the Gandharvas, attended by a thousand women.

sanskrit: raukmiṇeyaś ca sāmbaś ca kṣībau samaradurmadau divyamālyāmbaradharau vijahrāte 'marāv iva
english: Rukmiṇī's son and Sāmba, both exhilarated and terrible in battle, wearing divine garlands and garments, sported there like two immortals.

sanskrit: akrūraḥ sāraṇaś caiva gado bhānur viḍūrathaḥ niśaṭhaś cārudeṣṇaś ca pṛthur vipṛthur eva ca
english: Akrūra, Sāraṇa, Gada, Bhānu, Viḍūratha, Niśaṭha, Cārudeṣṇa, Pṛthu and Vipṛthu —

sanskrit: satyakaḥ sātyakiś caiva bhaṅgakārasahācarau hārdikyaḥ kṛtavarmā ca ye cānye nānukīrtitāḥ
english: Satyaka, Sātyaki, and Bhangakara's companions, Hārdikya Kṛtavarman, and many others not named here —

sanskrit: ete parivṛtāḥ strībhir gandharvaiś ca pṛthak pṛthak tam utsavaṃ raivatake śobhayāṃ cakrire tadā
english: all these, each accompanied by women and Gandharvas separately, adorned that festival on mount Raivataka at that time.

sanskrit: tadā kolāhale tasmin vartamāne mahāśubhe vāsudevaś ca pārthaś ca sahitau parijagmatuḥ
english: While that great and auspicious tumult was in progress, Vāsudeva and Pārtha wandered about together.

sanskrit: tatra caṅkramyamāṇau tau vāsudevasutāṃ śubhām alaṃkṛtāṃ sakhīmadhye bhadrāṃ dadṛśatus tadā
english: As the two strolled there, they beheld at that moment Vāsudeva's daughter Bhadra, fair and adorned, in the midst of her companions.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvaiva tām arjunasya kandarpaḥ samajāyata taṃ tathaikāgramanasaṃ kṛṣṇaḥ pārtham alakṣayat
english: The moment Arjuna saw her, Kāma arose within him; and Kṛṣṇa noticed Pārtha thus with his mind fixed single-pointedly upon her.

sanskrit: athābravīt puṣkarākṣaḥ prahasann iva bhārata vanecarasya kim idaṃ kāmenāloḍyate manaḥ
english: Then the lotus-eyed one spoke, almost smiling, O Bhārata: "Why is the mind of this forest-dweller now stirred by desire?"

sanskrit: mamaiṣā bhaginī pārtha sāraṇasya sahodarā yadi te vartate buddhir vakṣyāmi pitaraṃ svayam
english: "This is my sister, O Pārtha, the full sister of Sāraṇa; if the thought abides in your mind, I shall speak to my father myself."

sanskrit: arjuna uvāca duhitā vasudevasya vāsudevasya ca svasā rūpeṇa caiva saṃpannā kam ivaiṣā na mohayet
english: Arjuna said: She is the daughter of Vāsudeva and the sister of Vāsudeva; endowed with such beauty, whom would she not bewitch?

sanskrit: kṛtam eva tu kalyāṇaṃ sarvaṃ mama bhaved dhruvam yadi syān mama vārṣṇeyī mahiṣīyaṃ svasā tava
english: All good fortune would surely be mine if this lady of the Vṛṣṇi clan, your sister, were to become my principal queen.

sanskrit: prāptau tu ka upāyaḥ syāt tad bravīhi janārdana āsthāsyāmi tathā sarvaṃ yadi śakyaṃ nareṇa tat
english: But what means could there be of obtaining her — tell me, Janārdana; I will undertake everything, if it is achievable by a man.

sanskrit: vāsudeva uvāca svayaṃvaraḥ kṣatriyāṇāṃ vivāhaḥ puruṣarṣabha sa ca saṃśayitaḥ pārtha svabhāvasyānimittataḥ
english: Vāsudeva said: The svayamvara is the marriage form of Kṣatriyas, O bull among men; yet that too, O Pārtha, is uncertain because of the unpredictability of her own inclination.

sanskrit: prasahya haraṇaṃ cāpi kṣatriyāṇāṃ praśasyate vivāhahetoḥ śūrāṇām iti dharmavido viduḥ
english: Forcible abduction is also praised among Kṣatriyas for the purpose of marriage, among heroes — so those who know dharma declare.

sanskrit: sa tvam arjuna kalyāṇīṃ prasahya bhaginīṃ mama hara svayaṃvare hy asyāḥ ko vai veda cikīrṣitam
english: Therefore, Arjuna, you yourself forcibly carry off my auspicious sister; for who can know what she intends in a svayamvara?

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tato 'rjunaś ca kṛṣṇaś ca viniścityetikṛtyatām śīghragān puruṣān rājan preṣayām āsatus tadā
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then Arjuna and Kṛṣṇa, having resolved on the course of action, dispatched swift messengers, O king, at that time.

sanskrit: dharmarājāya tat sarvam indraprasthagatāya vai śrutvaiva ca mahābāhur anujajñe sa pāṇḍavaḥ
english: All of this was conveyed to Dharmarāja at Indraprastha, and that mighty-armed Pāṇḍava, having heard it, gave his consent.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca tataḥ saṃvādite tasminn anujñāto dhanaṃjayaḥ gatāṃ raivatake kanyāṃ viditvā janamejaya
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: Then, O Janamejaya, once agreement was reached and Dhanañjaya had received permission, learning that the maiden had gone to mount Raivataka —

sanskrit: vāsudevābhyanujñātaḥ kathayitvetikṛtyatām kṛṣṇasya matam ājñāya prayayau bharatarṣabhaḥ
english: permitted by Vāsudeva, having announced the plan of action, and knowing Kṛṣṇa's intent, that bull of the Bhārata line set forth.

sanskrit: rathena kāñcanāṅgena kalpitena yathāvidhi sainyasugrīvayuktena kiṅkiṇījālamālinā
english: On a chariot with golden fittings, properly equipped, yoked with the horses Sainya and Sugrīva, and adorned with a net of small bells —

sanskrit: sarvaśastropapannena jīmūtaravanādinā jvalitāgniprakāśena dviṣatāṃ harṣaghātinā
english: furnished with every weapon, thundering like a cloud in a forest, blazing bright as a burning fire, the slayer of enemies' joy —

sanskrit: saṃnaddhaḥ kavacī khaḍgī baddhagodhāṅgulitravān mṛgayāvyapadeśena yaugapadyena bhārata
english: fully armored, wearing his cuirass, sword at his side, wrist-guard and finger-guard fastened on — under the pretext of a hunt, simultaneously, O Bhārata.

sanskrit: subhadrā tv atha śailendram abhyarcya saha raivatam daivatāni ca sarvāṇi brāhmaṇān svasti vācya ca
english: Meanwhile Subhadrā, having worshipped the lord of mountains Raivataka together with all the deities, and having received the blessings of the Brāhmaṇas —

sanskrit: pradakṣiṇaṃ giriṃ kṛtvā prayayau dvārakāṃ prati tām abhidrutya kaunteyaḥ prasahyāropayad ratham
english: having circumambulated the mountain clockwise, was proceeding toward Dvārakā; Kaunteya rushed upon her and forcibly lifted her onto the chariot.

sanskrit: tataḥ sa puruṣavyāghras tām ādāya śucismitām rathenākāśagenaiva prayayau svapuraṃ prati
english: Then that tiger among men, taking her of the pure smile, sped away on that sky-coursing chariot toward his own city.

sanskrit: hriyamāṇāṃ tu tāṃ dṛṣṭvā subhadrāṃ sainiko janaḥ vikrośan prādravat sarvo dvārakām abhitaḥ purīm
english: Seeing Subhadrā being carried away, the soldiers all ran crying out in all directions toward the city of Dvārakā.

sanskrit: te samāsādya sahitāḥ sudharmām abhitaḥ sabhām sabhāpālasya tat sarvam ācakhyuḥ pārthavikramam
english: Coming together, they reached the assembly hall of Sudharma and reported to the hall-guardian everything of Pārtha's bold act.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ śrutvā sabhāpālo bherīṃ sāṃnāhikīṃ tataḥ samājaghne mahāghoṣāṃ jāmbūnadapariṣkṛtām
english: Hearing their report, the hall-guardian then struck the great war drum, loud-sounding, adorned with gold.

sanskrit: kṣubdhās tenātha śabdena bhojavṛṣṇyandhakās tadā annapānam apāsyātha samāpetuḥ sabhāṃ tataḥ
english: Stirred by that sound, the Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis, and Andhakas then flung aside their food and drink and flocked to the assembly.

sanskrit: tato jāmbūnadāṅgāni spardhyāstaraṇavanti ca maṇividrumacitrāṇi jvalitāgniprabhāṇi ca
english: Then with golden frames, spread with costly coverings, inlaid with gems and coral, blazing with a fiery radiance —

sanskrit: bhejire puruṣavyāghrā vṛṣṇyandhakamahārathāḥ siṃhāsanāni śataśo dhiṣṇyānīva hutāśanāḥ
english: the great warrior Vṛṣṇi and Andhaka heroes, tigers among men, occupied the hundreds of thrones like fires upon their altars.

sanskrit: teṣāṃ samupaviṣṭānāṃ devānām iva saṃnaye ācakhyau ceṣṭitaṃ jiṣṇoḥ sabhāpālaḥ sahānugaḥ
english: When they were seated, like the assembly of gods, the hall-guardian and his attendants reported to them the deed of Jiṣṇu.

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vṛṣṇivīrās te madaraktāntalocanāḥ amṛṣyamāṇāḥ pārthasya samutpetur ahaṃkṛtāḥ
english: Hearing that, those Vṛṣṇi heroes, their eyes reddened at the corners with pride and wine, unable to endure it, rose up in arrogance against Pārtha.

sanskrit: yojayadhvaṃ rathān āśu prāsān āharateti ca dhanūṃṣi ca mahārhāṇi kavacāni bṛhanti ca
english: "Yoke the chariots quickly!" and "Bring the lances!" and "Bring the great bows and the broad coats of mail!" —

sanskrit: sūtān uccukruśuḥ kec cid rathān yojayateti ca svayaṃ ca turagān ke cin ninyur hemavibhūṣitān
english: some cried out to the charioteers "Yoke the chariots!" and some themselves led out the horses adorned with gold.

sanskrit: ratheṣv ānīyamāneṣu kavaceṣu dhvajeṣu ca abhikrande nṛvīrāṇāṃ tadāsīt saṃkulaṃ mahat
english: With chariots being brought, coats of mail and banners being borne out, and the war-cries of the warrior-heroes, there was a great tumult at that time.

sanskrit: vanamālī tataḥ kṣībaḥ kailāsaśikharopamaḥ nīlavāsā madotsikta idaṃ vacanam abravīt
english: Then Vanamali, intoxicated, resembling the peak of Mount Kailāsa, clad in blue, swelling with exhilaration, spoke these words:

sanskrit: kim idaṃ kuruthāprajñās tūṣṇīṃ bhūte janārdane asya bhāvam avijñāya saṃkruddhā moghagarjitāḥ
english: "What are you doing, you imprudent ones? While Janārdana sits silent, you are in a rage without knowing his mind — these are empty roarings."

sanskrit: eṣa tāvad abhiprāyam ākhyātu svaṃ mahāmatiḥ yad asya rucitaṃ kartuṃ tat kurudhvam atandritāḥ
english: "Let this one of great wisdom first declare his own intention; whatever pleases him to do, that do you carry out without delay."

sanskrit: tatas te tad vacaḥ śrutvā grāhyarūpaṃ halāyudhāt tūṣṇīṃ bhūtās tataḥ sarve sādhu sādhv iti cābruvan
english: Then they, hearing that speech from Halaayudha — acceptable in its form — all fell silent, and said "Well said, well said."

sanskrit: samaṃ vaco niśamyeti baladevasya dhīmataḥ punar eva sabhāmadhye sarve tu samupāviśan
english: Having heard the balanced words of wise Baladeva, all of them sat down again in the midst of the assembly.

sanskrit: tato 'bravīt kāmapālo vāsudevaṃ paraṃtapam kim avāg upaviṣṭo 'si prekṣamāṇo janārdana
english: Then Kamapala addressed Vāsudeva the scorcher of foes: "Why do you sit silent and merely watching, Janārdana?"

sanskrit: satkṛtas tvatkṛte pārthaḥ sarvair asmābhir acyuta na ca so 'rhati tāṃ pūjāṃ durbuddhiḥ kulapāṃsanaḥ
english: "Pārtha was honored by all of us out of regard for you, O Acyuta, and yet that evil-minded defiler of his lineage does not deserve such honor."

sanskrit: ko hi tatraiva bhuktvānnaṃ bhājanaṃ bhettum arhati manyamānaḥ kule jātam ātmānaṃ puruṣaḥ kva cit
english: "For what man who considers himself born in a noble family would think it right to break the very vessel in which he has just eaten?"

sanskrit: īpsamānaś ca saṃbandhaṃ kṛtapūrvaṃ ca mānayan ko hi nāma bhavenārthī sāhasena samācaret
english: "And who, desiring a connection and honoring one already formed, could act in so reckless a manner as to call himself a man of honor?"

sanskrit: so 'vamanya ca nāmāsmān anādṛtya ca keśavam prasahya hṛtavān adya subhadrāṃ mṛtyum ātmanaḥ
english: "He, having insulted us and disregarded Keśava, has today forcibly carried off Subhadrā — it is his own death that he has seized."

sanskrit: kathaṃ hi śiraso madhye padaṃ tena kṛtaṃ mama marṣayiṣyāmi govinda pādasparśam ivoragaḥ
english: "How can I endure the foot he has placed upon the very crown of my head, O Govinda — as a serpent endures the touch of a foot?"

sanskrit: adya niṣkauravām ekaḥ kariṣyāmi vasuṃdharām na hi me marṣaṇīyo 'yam arjunasya vyatikramaḥ
english: "Today I alone will make the earth free of Kauravas; this transgression of Arjuna is not to be tolerated by me."

sanskrit: taṃ tathā garjamānaṃ tu meghadundubhiniḥsvanam anvapadyanta te sarve bhojavṛṣṇyandhakās tadā
english: Him thus roaring like the thunder of a great drum of clouds, all the Bhojas, Vṛṣṇis, and Andhakas then followed at that time.

sanskrit: vaiśaṃpāyana uvāca uktavanto yadā vākyam asakṛt sarvavṛṣṇayaḥ tato 'bravīd vāsudevo vākyaṃ dharmārthasaṃhitam
english: Vaiśaṃpāyana said: When all the Vṛṣṇis had spoken their words more than once, then Vāsudeva spoke words full of righteousness and purpose:

sanskrit: nāvamānaṃ kulasyāsya guḍākeśaḥ prayuktavān saṃmāno 'bhyadhikas tena prayukto 'yam asaṃśayam
english: "Guḍākeśa has not offered any insult to this family; rather, a higher honor has been shown by him — of this there is no doubt."

sanskrit: arthalubdhān na vaḥ pārtho manyate sātvatān sadā svayaṃvaram anādhṛṣyaṃ manyate cāpi pāṇḍavaḥ
english: "Pārtha does not regard you Sātvatas as greedy for gain; the Pāṇḍava also considers a svayamvara something not to be resisted, for him."

sanskrit: pradānam api kanyāyāḥ paśuvat ko 'numaṃsyate vikrayaṃ cāpy apatyasya kaḥ kuryāt puruṣo bhuvi
english: "Who would sanction the gift of a maiden as though she were cattle? And what man on earth would make a sale of his own offspring?"

sanskrit: etān doṣāṃś ca kaunteyo dṛṣṭavān iti me matiḥ ataḥ prasahya hṛtavān kanyāṃ dharmeṇa pāṇḍavaḥ
english: "It is my belief that Kaunteya saw these faults; it is for this reason that the Pāṇḍava carried off the maiden by force, and with dharma on his side."

sanskrit: ucitaś caiva saṃbandhaḥ subhadrā ca yaśasvinī eṣa cāpīdṛśaḥ pārthaḥ prasahya hṛtavān iti
english: "And this alliance is fitting, and Subhadrā is illustrious; and Pārtha himself is of such quality — it is for these reasons he has carried her off by force."

sanskrit: bharatasyānvaye jātaṃ śaṃtanoś ca mahātmanaḥ kuntibhojātmajāputraṃ ko bubhūṣeta nārjunam
english: "Born in the lineage of Bharata and of the great-souled Śaṃtanu, the grandson of Kuntibhoja's daughter — who would not wish for Arjuna?"

sanskrit: na ca paśyāmi yaḥ pārthaṃ vikrameṇa parājayet api sarveṣu lokeṣu sendrarudreṣu māriṣa
english: "And I see no one who could defeat Pārtha by valor, even in all the worlds, O noble ones, including those of Indra and Rudra."

sanskrit: sa ca nāma rathas tādṛṅ madīyās te ca vājinaḥ yoddhā pārthaś ca śīghrāstraḥ ko nu tena samo bhavet
english: "And that chariot of mine, and those horses of mine, and Pārtha as a fighter swift with his weapons — who could be a match for him?"

sanskrit: tam anudrutya sāntvena parameṇa dhanaṃjayam nivartayadhvaṃ saṃhṛṣṭā mamaiṣā paramā matiḥ
english: "Pursue Dhanañjaya and turn him back with the highest conciliation — this is my paramount counsel, and you should follow it gladly."

sanskrit: yadi nirjitya vaḥ pārtho balād gacchet svakaṃ puram praṇaśyed vo yaśaḥ sadyo na tu sāntve parājayaḥ
english: "If Pārtha were to conquer you and depart by force to his own city, your glory would instantly be destroyed; but in conciliation there is no defeat."

sanskrit: tac chrutvā vāsudevasya tathā cakrur janādhipa nivṛttaś cārjunas tatra vivāhaṃ kṛtavāṃs tataḥ
english: Hearing that, they acted accordingly, O lord of the people; and Arjuna turned back, and there performed the marriage.

sanskrit: uṣitvā tatra kaunteyaḥ saṃvatsaraparāḥ kṣapāḥ puṣkareṣu tataḥ śiṣṭaṃ kālaṃ vartitavān prabhuḥ pūrṇe tu dvādaśe varṣe khāṇḍavaprastham āviśat
english: Kaunteya dwelt there for more than a year of nights, then the lord spent the remaining time at the Puṣkara tirthas; and when the full twelve years were completed, he entered Khāṇḍavaprastha.

sanskrit: abhigamya sa rājānaṃ vinayena samāhitaḥ abhyarcya brāhmaṇān pārtho draupadīm abhijagmivān
english: Approaching the king with due humility and self-restraint, and having honored the Brāhmaṇas, Pārtha came to Draupadī.

sanskrit: taṃ draupadī pratyuvāca praṇayāt kurunandanam tatraiva gaccha kaunteya yatra sā sātvatātmajā subaddhasyāpi bhārasya pūrvabandhaḥ ślathāyate
english: Draupadī replied to that delighter of the Kurus with affection: "Go there, O Kaunteya, where that daughter of the Sātvata is; even a firmly tied knot loosens first at the old binding."

sanskrit: tathā bahuvidhaṃ kṛṣṇāṃ vilapantīṃ dhanaṃjayaḥ sāntvayām āsa bhūyaś ca kṣamayām āsa cāsakṛt
english: Dhanañjaya consoled Kṛṣṇā who was lamenting in many ways, and time and again besought her forgiveness.

sanskrit: subhadrāṃ tvaramāṇaś ca raktakauśeyavāsasam pārthaḥ prasthāpayām āsa kṛtvā gopālikāvapuḥ
english: And Pārtha, acting swiftly, dressed Subhadrā in red silk garments and sent her forward disguised in the form of a cowherdess.

sanskrit: sādhikaṃ tena rūpeṇa śobhamānā yaśasvinī bhavanaṃ śreṣṭham āsādya vīrapatnī varāṅganā vavande pṛthutāmrākṣī pṛthāṃ bhadrā yaśasvinī
english: Radiant beyond measure in that form, the illustrious one, wife of a hero and a beautiful woman, reaching the finest dwelling, Bhadra of wide copper-red eyes, that illustrious one, bowed to Pṛthā.

sanskrit: tato 'bhigamya tvaritā pūrṇendusadṛśānanā vavande draupadīṃ bhadrā preṣyāham iti cābravīt
english: Then Bhadra, her face like the full moon, quickly approached and bowed to Draupadī, saying: "I am your servant."

sanskrit: pratyutthāya ca tāṃ kṛṣṇā svasāraṃ mādhavasya tām sasvaje cāvadat prītā niḥsapatno 'stu te patiḥ tathaiva muditā bhadrā tām uvācaivam astv iti
english: And Kṛṣṇā, rising to meet her, embraced that sister of Mādhava, and spoke in delight: "May your husband be without a rival!" And Bhadra, equally gladdened, said: "So be it."

sanskrit: tatas te hṛṣṭamanasaḥ pāṇḍaveyā mahārathāḥ kuntī ca paramaprītā babhūva janamejaya
english: Then those great warrior Pāṇḍavas were gladdened in their hearts, and Kuntī was supremely delighted, O Janamejaya.

sanskrit: śrutvā tu puṇḍarīkākṣaḥ saṃprāptaṃ svapurottamam arjunaṃ pāṇḍavaśreṣṭham indraprasthagataṃ tadā
english: Hearing that Arjuna, best of the Pāṇḍavas, had arrived at his excellent city and had gone to Indraprastha —

sanskrit: ājagāma viśuddhātmā saha rāmeṇa keśavaḥ vṛṣṇyandhakamahāmātraiḥ saha vīrair mahārathaiḥ
english: Keśava of the pure soul came together with Rāma, accompanied by the great ministers and the heroic great warriors of the Vṛṣṇis and Andhakas.

sanskrit: bhrātṛbhiś ca kumāraiś ca yodhaiś ca śataśo vṛtaḥ sainyena mahatā śaurir abhiguptaḥ paraṃtapaḥ
english: Encircled by his brothers and young princes and by warriors in their hundreds, the Śauri, that scorcher of foes, was guarded by a great army.

sanskrit: tatra dānapatir dhīmān ājagāma mahāyaśāḥ akrūro vṛṣṇivīrāṇāṃ senāpatir ariṃdamaḥ
english: There too came the wise and greatly renowned lord of gifts, Akrūra, the commander of the Vṛṣṇi heroes, the subduer of enemies.

sanskrit: anādhṛṣṭir mahātejā uddhavaś ca mahāyaśāḥ sākṣād bṛhaspateḥ śiṣyo mahābuddhir mahāyaśāḥ
english: Anādhṛṣṭi of great splendor, and Uddhava of great fame — the very pupil of Bṛhaspati, of great intellect and great renown.

sanskrit: satyakaḥ sātyakiś caiva kṛtavarmā ca sātvataḥ pradyumnaś caiva sāmbaś ca niśaṭhaḥ śaṅkur eva ca
english: Satyaka and Sātyaki, and Kṛtavarman the Sātvata, Pradyumna and Sāmba, and Niśaṭha and Śaṅku —

sanskrit: cārudeṣṇaś ca vikrānto jhillī vipṛthur eva ca sāraṇaś ca mahābāhur gadaś ca viduṣāṃ varaḥ
english: the valiant Cārudeṣṇa, Jhilli, and Vipṛthu, and the mighty-armed Sāraṇa, and Gada the foremost among the wise —

sanskrit: ete cānye ca bahavo vṛṣṇibhojāndhakās tathā ājagmuḥ khāṇḍavaprastham ādāya haraṇaṃ bahu
english: these and many others among the Vṛṣṇis, Bhojas, and Andhakas came to Khāṇḍavaprastha, bringing with them abundant wedding gifts.

sanskrit: tato yudhiṣṭhiro rājā śrutvā mādhavam āgatam pratigrahārthaṃ kṛṣṇasya yamau prāsthāpayat tadā
english: Then King Yudhiṣṭhira, hearing that Mādhava had arrived, sent forth the twin brothers at that time to receive Kṛṣṇa with due honor.
